findings.claim: Removing `ctx.intersections.push(allOf)` disables the post-pass folding of intersection `allOf` arrays, which is a real behavior change in emitted JSON Schema.
findings.rationale: The deleted comment explicitly documents that `finalize` folds every object that holds this array (`foldIntersection`), and that registration is done here because the array identity is the handle shared with inheriting wrappers. With the push gone, no intersection ever reaches the fold pass, so results that previously collapsed to a single merged object (or merged into a wrapper/$ref-inheriting schema) will now be emitted as raw `allOf: [...]`. That changes output for every `z.intersection(...)` / `.and(...)` conversion and can break consumers that relied on the folded shape. Unless a compensating change exists elsewhere in this PR (I cannot see the rest of the diff, so confidence is moderate), this looks like an unintended regression.

findings.claim: `ctx.intersections` may now be a write-never collection, leaving dead state and a no-op fold pass in `finalize`.
findings.rationale: If this was the only producer for `ctx.intersections`, the field is now always empty and the `foldIntersection` loop in `finalize` becomes dead code, along with the context field and its type declaration. Worth verifying whether other producers exist; if not, the leftovers should be removed together or the push restored. Lower confidence since I only see this hunk.
